manufacturer.description: A company that manufactures HVAC equipment, used as the identity scope for model numbers and SKUs and as the subject of `manufactures` relationships.

properties.name: product_type
properties.description: Equipment categories this manufacturer is observed to produce. Derived from the `manufactures` edges rather than asserted by any source, so it is always consistent with the catalogue actually held.

quality_rules.description: A manufacturer with no models is an extraction artifact — usually a brand string that should have been an alias of an existing manufacturer.
Guards against an abbreviation ("ACS") winning canonical-name selection over the full legal name.

equipment_model.description: A specific HVAC equipment model as manufactured and sold, identified by its outdoor-unit model number and certified performance ratings.

properties.name: product_type
properties.description: Controlled equipment category. Mapped from source wording by normalizers/04-ontology-mapping.yaml; source wording is retained.

properties.name: cooling_capacity_btu
properties.description: Nominal cooling capacity in BTU per hour. Directly published by the manufacturer feed and the ratings directory; DERIVED from tonnage where a source publishes only tons (12000 BTU/h = 1 ton, exact by definition).

properties.name: nominal_tonnage
properties.description: Nominal cooling capacity in refrigeration tons. The unit the trade actually speaks in. Directly published by distributor listings and spec sheets; DERIVED from BTU/h elsewhere.

properties.name: seer2
properties.description: Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio 2. Dimensionless. The single most contested property in this vertical: manufacturer marketing figures and certified directory ratings routinely disagree, and the directory wins (see normalizers/fact-selection.yaml).

properties.name: eer2
properties.description: Energy Efficiency Ratio 2, at rated conditions. Dimensionless.

properties.name: hspf2
properties.description: Heating Seasonal Performance Factor 2. Heat pumps only — absent on cooling-only equipment, which is correct absence, not missing data.

properties.name: refrigerant
properties.description: Refrigerant designation, normalized to ASHRAE hyphenated form (`R-410A`). Commercially critical: the A2L transition means refrigerant type decides whether a replacement is a drop-in or a system change.

properties.name: voltage
properties.description: Nominal supply voltage. Normalized from notations like "208/230-1-60".

properties.name: phase
properties.description: Supply phase count (1 or 3). Parsed from the same notation as voltage.

properties.name: stage_count
properties.description: Number of compressor capacity stages.

properties.name: sound_level_db
properties.description: Rated sound level. Published on spec sheets and repeated — often inaccurately — by distributors. A standing source of conflict.

properties.name: weight_lb
properties.description: Net operating weight of the outdoor unit.

quality_rules.description: 12000 BTU/h = 1 ton, exact by definition. If a source's BTU figure and a different source's tonnage figure disagree by more than half a percent, one of them is describing a different unit and both are suspect.
SEER2 is a seasonal average and EER2 a peak-condition rating, so SEER2 above EER2 is expected. The reverse almost always means the two columns were swapped during extraction.
Applied to the NORMALIZED alias value, not the source spelling.

certification.description: A certified equipment ratings record published by a ratings directory, carrying the rated performance values and the certification's validity window.

properties.name: product_type
properties.description: Equipment category as classified by the certifying body.

properties.name: cooling_capacity_btu
properties.description: Certified cooling capacity, as rated.

properties.name: seer2
properties.description: Certified SEER2. This is the authoritative value for the linked equipment model — see normalizers/fact-selection.yaml `authoritative_by_property`.

properties.name: eer2
properties.description: Certified EER2.

properties.name: hspf2
properties.description: Certified HSPF2. Heat pumps only.

properties.name: refrigerant
properties.description: Refrigerant as recorded on the certification.

quality_rules.description: A certification nobody points at is an orphan — either the model number failed to resolve, or the directory carries a product we do not hold. Both are worth seeing.

sources.notes: The manufacturer feed. Uniquely provides: manufacturer SKU, series name, electrical characteristics (voltage/phase), compressor stage count, and the lifecycle block carrying `replaced_by` — the only source that asserts supersession, and therefore the only source that can answer this vertical's highest-value question. Omits sound level, UPC and certification references entirely. Publishes SEER2 as a marketing figure, which is why fact-selection.yaml prefers the certification directory for that property.

rights_policy.geographic_notes: Not applicable. Synthetic fixture data authored by the Data Foundry team.

acquisition_policy.notes: Direct HTTPS GET of individual PDF documents linked from model pages. Text-layer extraction only; the fixture PDF is generated with a real text layer so extraction is genuinely exercised rather than stubbed. No OCR path is approved — a scanned spec sheet would be a different acquisition decision with different accuracy characteristics, and would need its own review.

image_attribution.text: Dimensional drawings © Acme Climate Systems (synthetic test source).

sources.notes: Engineering spec sheets for the current Acme line (24ACC636A003, 24ACC648A003, 24ACC660A003). Uniquely provides sound level and net weight, and is the only source publishing nominal tonnage and BTU/h side by side — which makes it the reference for validating the 12000 BTU/h = 1 ton conversion rather than trusting it. Covers only three current models: no discontinued units, no other manufacturers, no UPC, no certification reference. Disagrees with coolsupply-distributor on sound level for 24ACC648A003 (72 dB published vs 69 dB listed) and wins on authority, 90 to 45.

rights_policy.geographic_notes: Not applicable. Synthetic fixture data authored by the Data Foundry team. Recorded because a real ratings directory would carry directory-specific redistribution terms that would need reading before any of this were true.

Preferring the published bulk file over crawling the directory's search UI is both cheaper and the behaviour the publisher intends. In the fixture harness this reads fixtures/ahri-export.csv from disk.

license_split.notes: Data licence only; no code is vendored from this source.

sources.notes: The authority for certified performance and the only source spanning all three manufacturers, which makes it the backbone of cross-manufacturer comparison. Uniquely provides the certification reference (`ahri_ref`) and the certified SEER2/EER2/HSPF2 values. Omits electrical data, sound level, weight and UPC entirely. Formats model numbers inconsistently BY MANUFACTURER — spaces for Acme (`24ACC6 36A003`), plain for Northwind, hyphenated for Borealis — which is realistic and is the main workout for identifier normalization. Drops discontinued models from each export, so the gen-1 and gen-2 Acme units in the supersession chain appear in no certification record at all.

attribution_requirement.text: Listing data courtesy of CoolSupply Wholesale (synthetic test source).

rights_policy.publisher_legal_entity: CoolSupply Wholesale (fictional entity; synthetic test data)

attribution.text: Listing data courtesy of CoolSupply Wholesale (synthetic test source).

rights_policy.geographic_notes: Not applicable. Synthetic fixture data authored by the Data Foundry team. Noted here because a real distributor catalogue in the EU/UK would raise a sui generis database right question that this synthetic stand-in does not.

acquisition_policy.notes: Requires a rendering acquisition adapter (Cloudflare Browser Run or Crawl4AI — swappable, per AGENTS.md rule 6; the registry declares the permitted METHOD, never the vendor). Approval covers rendering public product pages only: no cart, account or search paths, matching the robots snapshot above. Rendering permission is a rights decision, not a technical one — "we could render it" is not "we may render it".

license_split.notes: No licence is offered by the publisher. Facts are used under the AMBER classification pending business review; the page markup itself is not republished.

sources.notes: The only source of UPCs, and a useful independent corroborator on capacity and refrigerant. Everything it publishes should be treated as re-keyed rather than authoritative: it lists capacity in tons ("3 Ton"), lowercases and hyphenates model numbers (`24acc6-36a003`), omits EER2/HSPF2/phase/stage count/weight, and disagrees with the manufacturer's own spec sheet on sound level for 24ACC648A003 (69 dB listed vs 72 dB published). That conflict is intentional and is what exercises authority-weighted fact selection. Its own item numbers (`CS-######`) are deliberately NOT ingested — they are source-scoped inventory codes with no cross-source meaning.

relationships.description: The only supersession assertion in the entire source set. No other source publishes replacement data, which is precisely why this vertical is worth building.

excluded_fields.reason: Pricing is volatile, source-specific and commercially sensitive. It is not a durable product fact and republishing it raises rights questions the fact model does not answer.
AGENTS.md rule 9. Recorded as a media_asset with its URL and rights status; NOT cached to R2, because this source's image_policy sets images_reusable false.

No canonical property exists for lifecycle state in the agreed vocabulary, and the graph already encodes it: a model with an inbound `supersedes` edge is superseded. Adding a `lifecycle_status` property would duplicate that as a denormalized fact that can drift out of agreement with the edge. See CHANGELOG.md "Proposed vocabulary additions".
Same. The date belongs on the `supersedes` edge as its `valid_from`, where it is already carried, rather than as a property of the model.
Feed-level metadata; recorded on the artifact, not as entity facts.

The distributor's own inventory code (`CS-######`). Source-scoped with no cross-source meaning — it is NOT a manufacturer SKU and recording it as one would attach a distributor's numbering to the manufacturer's identity.
A marketing brand under the same manufacturer. Resolved as a manufacturer alias rather than stored as a fact; treating it as a separate value would split one company into two entities.

Every row in the export is Active — discontinued models are dropped from each quarterly file. A single-valued column cannot discriminate anything, and the absence of a model from a later export is the real signal. Recorded on the artifact instead.

properties.label: Cooling Capacity
properties.description: This source publishes tonnage AND BTU/h on the same page, which is what lets `capacity_tonnage_consistency` validate the 12000 BTU/h = 1 ton conversion against published data instead of trusting it.

relationships.description: The publisher is the manufacturer, so the subject is a literal rather than an extracted field. Declared explicitly so the edge still carries evidence (the document itself) rather than being inferred silently.

excluded_fields.reason: Boilerplate, present on every page; not a product fact.

seer2.rationale: Certification and standards sources can report comparable test-procedure measurements. A regulatory filing is instead a manufacturer-reported value held by a regulator; it is not certification. All listed types enter the authority membership set, with conflicts resolved by source-specific field reliability or authority rank. Manufacturer marketing pages are excluded.

eer2.rationale: Same test-procedure argument as seer2, and the same filing caveat.

hspf2.rationale: Same test-procedure argument as seer2, and the same filing caveat.

cooling_capacity_btu.rationale: Certification, filing and manufacturer sources can each provide a primary capacity claim. They are equal at criterion 1; source-specific reliability or authority rank resolves any disagreement. Distributors are excluded: their capacity is usually inferred from the model number.

sound_level_db.rationale: No certification body in scope rates sound. The manufacturer's published spec sheet is the only primary measurement; everything else is a copy of it, and copies acquire errors.

weight_lb.rationale: Physical property, measured by whoever builds it.

voltage.rationale: Electrical characteristics come from the nameplate.

phase.rationale: Electrical characteristics come from the nameplate.

stage_count.rationale: A design characteristic, known only to the manufacturer.

refrigerant.rationale: All listed source types can provide a primary refrigerant claim and rarely disagree. Where they do, it usually signals a mid-production refrigerant change and should be escalated rather than silently resolved — see `escalate_on_conflict` below.

product_type.rationale: Each listed source can supply a primary product classification. They are equal at criterion 1; source-specific reliability or authority rank resolves taxonomy disagreements across publishers.

nominal_tonnage.rationale: Tonnage and capacity are the same measurement in different units, so the authoritative source is whoever published the capacity. The one real rule is that a stated value beats a computed one.

upc.note: The only source of UPCs, and barcodes are transcribed from the carton rather than re-keyed from a spec table. Checksum-validated on ingest.

sound_level_db.note: Demonstrably unreliable — the 69 dB listing for 24ACC648A003 contradicts the manufacturer's published 72 dB. Kept as a corroborating signal only.

seer2.note: Repeats manufacturer marketing figures rather than certified ratings.
Nominal/marketing figure. Reliable as a statement of what the manufacturer claims; not as a statement of certified performance.

supersedes.note: A manufacturer is the only possible authority on its own product line.

non_independent_pairs.reason: The distributor's spec table is transcribed from the manufacturer's published data. Their agreement on seer2 = 14.5 in Conflict A is one claim counted twice, not two independent confirmations.

consistency_checks.description: A certification whose capacity disagrees with the model's means the model number resolved to the wrong entity. Never resolve this by picking a value — break the join and escalate.

editorial_override.note: An override is a fact with its own evidence — a named human and a written reason — not a magic value. An entry missing either is ignored entirely; it does not quietly demote itself to a tiebreaker. Two entries competing for one property cancel out and the ordinary criteria decide instead.

convert_from.note: Exact by definition: one refrigeration ton is 12000 BTU/h. Not an approximation and not rounded — an inexact factor here would make the capacity/tonnage consistency check fail on correct data.
Approximate. No current source publishes kW; declared for completeness.
The exact reciprocal of 12000. Implementations should divide by 12000 rather than multiply by this decimal, which is written out only so the declaration is self-describing.

unit_conversions.note: dB and dB(A) are treated as the same canonical unit here because every source in this vertical publishes A-weighted sound ratings while labelling them inconsistently. If a source ever publishes unweighted dB this collapse becomes wrong and must be split.

derived_properties.description: Fills tonnage for acme-hvac-catalog and ahri-directory-export, which publish BTU/h only.
Fills BTU/h for coolsupply-distributor, which publishes "3 Ton" and nothing else.

identifier_rules.description: Uppercase and strip every separator. Deliberately aggressive: no source in this vertical uses separators meaningfully, so discarding them costs nothing and collapses all four observed spellings onto one key.
Certification reference. Sources write it bare (`20134501`) or prefixed (`AHRI 20134501`, `AHRI-20134501`); the digits are the identity.
Manufacturer ordering SKU. Hyphens are RETAINED here, unlike model numbers: `ACS-24ACC636A003` is a structured code whose prefix identifies the manufacturer, and flattening it would discard that.

Retail barcode, digits only, left-padded to 12. Supplied exclusively by coolsupply-distributor — a low-authority source holding a high-precision identifier, which is a good argument for keeping low-authority sources.
Marketing series. Narrows candidates; never asserts identity.

notation_rules.description: "208/230-1-60" is voltage-range / phase / frequency. Splits into two canonical properties; frequency is deliberately not modelled (see `excluded` below) because every unit in scope is 60 Hz and a property with one value cannot filter anything.

excluded.reason: Frequency is 60 Hz for every unit in scope. Modelling it would add a fact to every entity that no query could ever discriminate on.
Retained in fact_evidence.source_value as part of the full original notation, so the dual rating is recoverable without being a second fact.

notation_rules.description: "3 Ton", "36,000 BTU/h", "4.0 Tons" — a number and its unit in one cell. The unit decides which canonical property receives the value; the other is then filled by the derived_properties rules in Layer 2.
"72 dB", "187 lb" — strip the suffix, keep the unit for validation.

controlled_vocabularies.description: Equipment category. Sources describe the same box as a "Condenser", an "Air Conditioner" and a "Split System Air Conditioner" — one canonical term, because a filter with three synonymous options is a broken filter.

excluded.reason: Ductless systems are a genuinely different product class with different identity and compatibility rules. Mapping them onto air_conditioner would put incomparable equipment in the same filter. They need their own canonical term when the vertical expands, and that is a schema_version bump, not a synonym.

controlled_vocabularies.description: Normalized to ASHRAE hyphenated form. Commercially load-bearing: the A2L transition means refrigerant type decides whether a replacement is a drop-in or a system change, so `R410A` and `R-410A` colliding as separate filter values would break the single most important compatibility question in the vertical.

excluded.reason: A category label, not a designation. Extraction artifact.

fields.label: Equipment category
fields.rationale: The primary category split, and a genuine search intent in its own right ("3 ton heat pump"). Low cardinality, high demand, no duplication risk.

fields.label: Nominal tonnage
fields.rationale: The unit the trade actually searches in. "3 ton air conditioner" is a high-intent commercial query; "36000 BTU air conditioner" is not, even though they are the same filter.

fields.label: Cooling capacity

seo.reason: Filtering on BTU/h returns the SAME set as filtering on tonnage — they are one measurement in two units. Indexing both would create a near-duplicate page for every capacity. The tonnage facet is indexable; this one is UI and API only.

fields.rationale: Essential for engineering-precise API queries; redundant for SEO.

fields.label: SEER2
fields.rationale: Efficiency minimums are set by regional code, so "14.3 SEER2 or higher" is a real compliance question with real money attached. Conditional because most individual bucket/type combinations are thin.

seo.reason: Specialist filter with negligible search demand. UI and API only.
Specialist filter, and only applicable to a subset of the catalogue.

fields.label: Refrigerant
fields.rationale: The highest-demand facet in the vertical right now. The A2L transition means "R-454B air conditioner" is a live purchasing question for every contractor, and the answer decides whether a replacement is a drop-in or a system change.

seo.reason: A qualifier on another search, not a search. Nobody looks for "208 volt equipment"; they look for a 3-ton condenser that happens to be 208V.
Two values, both low-intent. Qualifier only.
Low cardinality and low standalone demand.

Coverage is thin (only two sources publish it) and the distributor's values are unreliable. A facet that silently drops most of the catalogue teaches users the data is incomplete. Revisit when coverage exceeds 80%.
Logistics detail. Sortable and queryable; never a landing page.

fields.label: Manufacturer
fields.rationale: Brand plus category is the highest-intent pattern in the vertical. The lower min_results reflects that a manufacturer page is legitimate even with a small catalogue — it is a real entity, not a generated combination.

indexable_combinations.rationale: "3 ton heat pump" is how contractors and homeowners actually search, and it is the single most common query pattern in the vertical.
"R-454B air conditioner" is a live compliance and compatibility question during the A2L transition, with a clear commercial decision behind it.
Brand-plus-category navigation. Distinct intent, distinct content, and a genuine entry point rather than a generated permutation.

The one three-field combination that earns a page: a contractor replacing a specific unit under the new refrigerant rules needs exactly this intersection. The raised min_results is what keeps it from becoming a permutation generator.

denied_combinations.reason: The same measurement in two units. Every such page is a duplicate of a tonnage page by construction.
Qualifiers, not intents. Would generate a page for every electrical configuration with no distinct user behind any of them.
Strongly correlated ratings. Combining them produces near-identical result sets across adjacent buckets.
Two thin-coverage properties. Their intersection is a page about almost nothing, backed by data we mostly do not have.

A hard ceiling. Beyond three facets the result sets are individually tiny and collectively near-duplicate — the exact failure mode rule 8 exists to prevent. Deeper filtering stays fully available in the UI and the API; it simply never becomes an indexable URL.
